correctness.rationale: Theorem 6.4 of arXiv:1108.4227v1 gives normalization fibers and immersion. At a d-orbit, derivative vectors are -G(Z)^(n/d-1) G(Z)/(Z-a_j). Evaluating the divided factors at the distinct roots a_k proves rank d (nonzero G prime values), valid even when the characteristic divides n/d. Distinct smooth branches with independent tangents formally straighten to d coordinate axes. Their normalization quotient has length d-1; the unit gluing quotient at the rational singularity with residue extension F_(q^d) is Res_(q^d/q) Gm/Gm, yielding the precise connected Picard torus over Fq. Rational point, extension count and zeta are checked against the source fiber theorem. Standalone exact finite-field orbit/rank checks and unrelated projective Hilbert computations replay successfully. These tests do not substitute for the uniform argument.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is transversality of arbitrary degree-d>=3 Frobenius-orbit branches on B_n and the exact all-n Picard-group structure. Original 2011 source supplies the map, normalization, immersion, and fibers, and thereby implies the stated extension-point/zeta formulas, so these are only corollaries. The 2014 study and classical nodal Picard theory concern n=2 plane nodal curves. No inspected primary work or mathematical record directly implies independence of distinct tangent directions in all higher B_n or the resulting no-unipotent Picard group. Historical priority remains subject to undiscovered specialist work.
residual_risks: A specialist thesis or later paper may already derive higher B_n local seminormality or its generalized Jacobian; absence from targeted searches does not certify historical novelty.
The zeta and extension-count formulas are implied by the 2011 normalization theorem and are not separately novel.

value.rationale: The family is a canonical symmetric-Frobenius construction of rational space curves over every finite field and arbitrary ambient dimension. The unresolved local question of whether distinct branches are tangent or transverse controls conductor, genus and toric versus additive Picard components, not merely a small numerical improvement. The result gives a uniform natural local classification and group isomorphism for every n>=3 (including p dividing n), together with concrete arithmetic invariants.
